modules.name: App Lifecycle & IPC Controller
modules.description: Core Wails desktop application controller, managing window lifecycle, menu actions, account switching, and IPC event dispatch.

modules.name: Background Mailbox Sync Engine
modules.description: Multi-account background worker orchestrating Google Gmail API polling, message fetching, delta synchronizations, and concurrency control.

modules.name: Local SQLite Store & FTS5 Search
modules.description: Embedded SQLite database layer handling accounts, threads, messages, attachments, full-text search indexing, and thread categorizations.

modules.name: HTML Email Sanitizer & Tracker Blocker
modules.description: Security pipeline for stripping tracking pixels (1x1 images), email marketing beacons, and untrusted scripts from HTML email bodies.

modules.name: OAuth2 Google Authentication Service
modules.description: Handles Google OAuth2 client secrets, local token persistence in ~/.fastmail, browser authorization flows, and token refresh.

modules.name: Svelte 5 Reactive Frontend
modules.description: Desktop user interface featuring split inbox views (Main, Newsletters, Updates), keyboard navigation shortcuts, theme toggle, and message reader.

func() {
	code := <-codeChan
	_ = srv.Shutdown(context.Background())
	a.EmitLog("INFO", "OAuth code received, exchanging for access token...")
	tok, err := a.auth.ExchangeCode(context.Background(), code)
	if err != nil {
		a.EmitLog("ERROR", fmt.Sprintf("Token exchange failed: %v", err))
		return
	}
	client, err := a.auth.NewGmailClient(context.Background(), tok)
	if err != nil {
		a.EmitLog("ERROR", fmt.Sprintf("Failed to initialize Gmail client: %v", err))
		return
	}
	email, err := a.auth.GetUserEmail(context.Background(), client)
	if err != nil {
		a.EmitLog("WARN", "Could not get email profile, fallback to user")
		email = fmt.Sprintf("account_%d@gmail.com", time.Now().Unix())
	}
	_ = a.auth.SaveTokenForAccount(email, tok)
	a.mu.Lock()
	a.clients[email] = client
	a.mu.Unlock()
	a.EmitLog("INFO", fmt.Sprintf("Account connected: %s. Starting background sync...", email))
	_ = a.SyncAccount(email)
	wailsRuntime.EventsEmit(a.ctx, "accounts:updated", a.GetAccounts())
}

hazards.description: Mutex mu is acquired inside a loop iteration. If not released each cycle, it causes immediate deadlock.
hazards.remedy: Acquire lock outside loop or ensure explicit unlock in each iteration body.

hazards.title: Mutex Locked Without Defer Unlock
hazards.description: Function 'startup' acquires a mutex without using 'defer mu.Unlock()'. Any early return or panic will leave the mutex permanently locked, deadlocking the app.
hazards.remedy: Immediately follow `mu.Lock()` with `defer mu.Unlock()` on the next line.

hazards.title: Goroutine Spawned Without Cancellation Context
hazards.description: Goroutine spawned in 'startup' does not pass or monitor context.Context. If the app is closed or sync canceled, this goroutine leaks in the background.
hazards.remedy: Pass ctx context.Context and select on case <-ctx.Done(): return.

hazards.title: Regex-Based HTML Email Sanitization (XSS Risk)
hazards.description: Email HTML is sanitized using regular expressions (`imgTagRegex`, `preheaderDivRegex`). Regex cannot reliably parse nested HTML or DOM mutation vectors, creating Stored XSS and tracking leak vulnerabilities.
hazards.remedy: Adopt tokenized DOM sanitization (e.g. `bluemonday.UGCPolicy()`).

hazards.title: SQL Query Constructed via String Concatenation
hazards.description: SQL query at line 416 uses fmt.Sprintf instead of prepared statement placeholders (`?`).
hazards.remedy: Use parameterized placeholders `?` in db.Query / db.Exec.

idiomExplainers.summary: A sync.Mutex provides exclusive mutual exclusion (1 writer at a time). A sync.RWMutex allows many concurrent readers (`RLock()`) OR 1 exclusive writer (`Lock()`).
idiomExplainers.whyItMatters: If multiple goroutines read email threads simultaneously, using RLock() allows full parallel CPU utilization without contention. Writers wait for readers to finish.
idiomExplainers.goRule: Never upgrade an RLock to a Lock on the same goroutine — it deadlocks immediately.

idiomExplainers.concept: Defer Statement Execution & Mutex Unlock Safety
idiomExplainers.summary: `defer` evaluates arguments immediately but delays execution until the surrounding function returns (in LIFO stack order).
idiomExplainers.whyItMatters: Using `defer mu.Unlock()` guarantees that even if a function returns early due to an error (`if err != nil { return }`) or panics, the mutex will always be unlocked.
idiomExplainers.goRule: Always put `defer mu.Unlock()` immediately after `mu.Lock()`. Never place defer inside a long loop.

idiomExplainers.concept: Go Concurrent Map Writes: Fatal Unrecoverable Panics
idiomExplainers.summary: Unlike Python or JS, standard Go `map[K]V` types are not thread-safe. Concurrent writes trigger an unrecoverable SIGSEGV/panic that bypasses `recover()`.
idiomExplainers.whyItMatters: AI-generated sync loops often spawn multiple background workers that modify `a.clients[account] = client`. Without mutex locks, this crashes the desktop app instantly.
idiomExplainers.goRule: All map accesses (reads, writes, deletes, len) must be guarded by a mutex, or use `sync.Map`.

idiomExplainers.summary: `context.Context` carries cancellation signals and timeouts across API boundaries and background goroutines.
idiomExplainers.whyItMatters: When the user switches mailboxes or quits the app, background sync goroutines must stop immediately rather than continuing to consume network bandwidth and battery.
idiomExplainers.goRule: Pass `ctx context.Context` as the first argument, and check `case <-ctx.Done(): return` inside long loops.

taintFlows.description: Raw untrusted HTML body ingested from Google API, passed through regex sanitizer, and stored in SQLite local database.
steps: sync.go:210 -> Gmail API returns raw MIME payload
sanitizer.go:50 -> SanitizeEmailHTML strips tracker patterns and bloat
store.go:180 -> LocalStore.InsertMessage executes parameterized INSERT INTO messages
frontend/src/App.svelte:120 -> Svelte renders cleanHTML via {@html message.body}

taintFlows.description: User search string passed from Svelte frontend to Go backend search handler.
steps: frontend/src/App.svelte -> User types query in search bar
store.go:320 -> LocalStore.SearchMessages uses parameterized query `SELECT * FROM messages WHERE messages MATCH ?`

bypassRisks: Nested Tag Bypass: `<scr<script>ipt>` survives regex removal.
Attribute Obfuscation: `` event handlers not completely tokenized.
Malformed HTML Mutation (mXSS): Browsers normalize malformed HTML differently than regex assumptions.
Tracking Pixel Circumvention: 1x1 image tags with dynamic base64 or custom query parameters bypass static URL regex patterns.
sanitizerAudits.recommendation: Replace regex-based string stripping with an AST-based HTML tokenizer/sanitizer like `microcosm-cc/bluemonday` or DOMPurify.

invariants.invariant: All Mutex Lock operations must be followed by defer Unlock
invariants.explanation: Found 2 methods where mutex is manually unlocked before returns instead of using defer.

invariants.invariant: Shared maps (`clients`, `syncingAccounts`) must have 100% mutex guard coverage
invariants.explanation: Map write in background sync callback lacks syncMu lock acquisition.

invariants.invariant: Untrusted Email HTML must pass through DOM-safe tokenizer before rendering
invariants.explanation: Sanitization relies on Regex which is susceptible to mXSS and nested script tag bypasses.

invariants.invariant: All SQLite queries must use parameterized placeholders (?)
invariants.explanation: All 18 SQL queries in store.go correctly use parameterized placeholders.

invariants.invariant: All Wails exposed methods must return an error tuple for frontend safety
invariants.explanation: All exported methods on App return `(Result, error)` matching Wails IPC standards.

summary: FastMail is a modern Wails v2 desktop email client built with a Go backend and Svelte frontend. It features multi-account Gmail sync, embedded SQLite with FTS5 search, HTML tracker blocking, and split inbox categorizations. Static analysis identified 2 critical concurrency hazards (concurrent map access in sync routines) and 1 critical security vulnerability (regex-based HTML sanitization bypasses).
